parsed.attack: A one-time purchase sold to 17-19 year olds is the worst possible shape against 2026 CPIs. At a typical GBP 5-8 ($7-10) price the net after the store fee is $5-7, so break-even on paid installs needs an install-to-purchase rate of about 97% on iOS ($5.84/$6) and 32% on Android ($1.92/$6); even pricing at $30 leaves an iOS break-even of 28% conversion. The paid channel is closed at every price a learner driver will pay, and invite_for_function does not fix it because the invited parent completes a household you already acquired rather than bringing a new one. The audience then exits permanently at the practical test - no renewal, no upsell - so 100% of the base is reacquired every year at a CAC the price cannot carry.
parsed.strongest_defence: Marginal cost is zero on-device, so a fully organic channel is all it needs: driving instructors, school word of mouth and DVSA-adjacent forums reaching even 5% of the ~750k UK practical-test candidates a year at GBP 7.99 is roughly $260k of near-100%-margin revenue with no ad spend at all.
parsed.verdict_reason: On-device inference removes the margin problem, but a sub-$10 one-time price makes break-even paid conversion 32-97%, so the product can only ever grow by free word of mouth among a cohort that fully churns each year.
